Scenario: You see your class valedictorian giving a perfect speech. You feel a pang of regret that that's not you. You remind yourself that success takes many forms, and you feel your regret ease.
Comprehension Question: Does your regret about not being valedictorian ease?

Scenario: You scroll through your feed and see everyone achieving things like getting into college and getting straight As in all their classes. You aren't planning to go to college next year, and you feel a pit of insecurity in your stomach. You wonder if you aren't as accomplished as your classmates. However, you also know that social media is a highlight reel that doesn't tell the whole story.
Comprehension Question: Do you fully believe you're less accomplished than your classmates?

Scenario: You didn't get any special recognition at the ceremony while your friends won multiple awards. You sink down into your seat, feeling invisible. As you see the smiling faces of your friends on stage, you feel proud of them.
Comprehension Question: You think your own achievements in school are....

Scenario: You are lying on the couch scrolling through social media. You see lots of posts about people achieving awards or internships. You feel a pinch of inadequacy, but remind yourself that your path doesn’t need to look like theirs, and you feel the pressure ease.
Comprehension Question: Do you still feel inadequate after comparing yourself to others online?

Scenario: Today, you will receive an important call. You'll find out if you got the job you interviewed for. As you think about waiting for the call, your anxiety is tolerable.
Comprehension Question: When you think about speaking on the phone, you feel...

Scenario: Your friend shares their test score on their story, showing they aced it. You bombed the same test and feel embarrassed. Then you remind yourself that one grade isn't your whole academic story, and you feel encouraged.
Comprehension Question: You think school is...
Correct Response: Not a competition with your friends

Scenario: You notice a friend has dozens of comments under their vacation post. You only got a handful, mostly from family. Then you remind yourself that attention online does not equal real-life support, and you feel secure.
Comprehension Question: The number of comments on your posts....
Correct Response: Can fluctuate based on many factors

Scenario: Your teacher is giving a verbal pop quiz during a morning class. You freeze when your teacher calls on you, even though you knew the answer last night. The teacher calls on someone else, and you feel your face burning, wondering if you just aren't smart enough to talk in class. When the teacher asks another question, you feel determind to rasie your hand again.
Comprehension Question: Are you determined to raise your hand again?

Scenario: Your teacher hands out an in-class assignment and lets you know it's graded for completion, not accuracy. As you read through the sheet you feel your cheeks heat up - you are confused and want to ask for help, but are embarrassed to raise your hand in the silent classroom.  You remind yourself that asking questions is part of learning, and calmly raise your hand.
Comprehension Question: When you need help in the future, you will...
Incorrect Response: Figure it out on your own

Scenario: Your teacher calls on you to answer a question about the book you just read. You don't know what to say, and your mind goes blank. After a few moments, you prepare your answer, knowing that no matter what answer you give, your teacher will probably appreciate your effort.
Comprehension Question: Your teacher probably thinks you are...

Scenario: Your group submits a big project without checking in with you. Your surprise quickly turns into insecurity, wondering if they finished without you because they think your work is bad. You think about the quality of your work on the assignment, and you feel confident.
Comprehension Question: You think your groupmates submitted early...
Correct Response: Because they wanted to get it in on time

Scenario: Your friends talk about high ACT scores. You worry your low score means you're not smart and feel your confidence fall sharply. You remind yourself that a single test won't make or break your entire application.
Comprehension Question: Standarized test scores...
Correct Response: Are an imperfect measure of one-time performance
Incorrect Response: Are an accuracte signal of intellegence

Scenario: You're working on math homework with a few friends. You say an answer to the first question, and your friend quickly notices a problem in your work and corrects your answer. As you are looking over your work, you realize you made a mistake, and that's okay.
Comprehension Question: Your friend is probably trying to...

Scenario: You're chosen to lead a small group project in your math class. As your group sits down together, you suddenly feel nervous about giving directions. You remind yourself leadership means learning, not perfection, and you feel confident.
Comprehension Question: When you think about being a leader, you feel...

Scenario: You watch classmates fly through a review worksheet while you're still on question three. You start to feel shame creep over you as you think about how everyone seems to learn faster than you. You remind yourself that understanding deeply takes time, and you feel forgiving of your pace.
Comprehension Question: You probably need....
Correct Response: Some extra support in this subject
Incorrect Response: To prepare to fail the class

Scenario: You watch classmates answer questions instantly. You worry you'll never catch up and feel dread settle in your chest. You remind yourself that everyone learns differently and you feel balanced.
Comprehension Question: Answering questions fast is...
Correct Response: Probably not directly related to your intellegence

Scenario: You walk into your first day at a new school, and no one talks to you right away. You start to think you won’t make friends. You remind yourself that meaningful connections take time, and you feel confident finding your seat.
Comprehension Question: In the future you will probably....

Scenario: You volunteer to mentor younger students at your school. When you show up to the first meeting and hear other mentors introduce themselves, you feel unsure if you have enough to offer. You remind yourself that being present is important.
Comprehension Question: Do you remind yourself that being present matters?

Scenario: You see a friend finish an essay days early while you're still on your outline. You start to think you're just slow. You remind yourself that working at your own pace can still lead to great results, and you feel steadier.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel steadier about working at your own pace?

Scenario: You really enjoy your English class, and you feel like you finally have a teacher who gets you. As you walk into class one morning, you feel a horrible shock, realizing you totally forgot to complete the essay due today. This memory lapse will probably not impact your teacher's impression of you.
Comprehension Question: Will forgetting the essay likely ruin your teacher's impression of you?

Scenario: You overhear classmates arguing about politics, and your chest tightens. You imagine conversations around you getting even sharper. It occurs to you that conversations lead to progress.
Comprehension Question: Do you think tense conversations can lead to progress?

Scenario: You notice your group hasn't done their parts, and the deadline is tomorrow. You start to think it’s all on you to save the grade. You remind yourself that you can only control your effort, not others’, and if they don't finish their work, the consequences will be on them.
Comprehension Question: Are you solely responsible for saving the group's grade?

Scenario: You look at your calendar packed with practice, homework, and club stuff, and it feels like too much all at once. You want to cut down on your non-essential commitments, but you feel guilty for canceling. You think people will probably be understanding of your choice.
Comprehension Question: Will people probably be understanding if you cut back on commitments?

Scenario: You hear your friends proudly talk about getting into highly ranked colleges. You feel embarrassed about applying mainly to local schools, and your stomach tightens. You remind yourself you'll grow wherever you go, and you start to feel enthusiastic.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel enthusiastic about your college choice?

Scenario: You hand in a late homework assignment to your teacher a few days after it is due. As you hand it to him, you hear him sigh, and feel your cheeks get hot. You think your teacher is sighing because he is tired.
Comprehension Question: Is your teacher sighing because of you?

Scenario: You got your report card today, and you got a couple of lower grades than you expected. Your friends are talking about their grades, and they said they got straight As. If you tell your friends your grades, they will be understanding.
Comprehension Question: Will your friends be understanding about your grades?

Scenario: You decide to run for class president, and you have to debate your fellow candidates in front of the school. The other candidates are on the debate team, and this is your first debate. When you think about arguing your position in front of your classmates, you feel confident.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel confident about the debate?

Scenario: You blank on an answer when the teacher calls on you. As the silence stretches out and you feel your classmates' eyes on you, you feel totally dumb. You remind yourself that everyone forgets things sometimes, and your classmates will quickly move on.
Comprehension Question: Will your classmates quickly move on after you blank on an answer?

Scenario: You ask your teacher a question during a loud class period. Your teacher doesn't acknowledge you, and you feel your face flush. Your question was probably unheard by your teacher.
Comprehension Question: Was your teacher ignoring your question on purpose?

Scenario: You are working on a group project in class, and everyone talks over you when you try to suggest an idea. You worry your ideas are terrible and feel your confidence drop sharply. You remind yourself that people sometimes interrupt you because they are distracted.
Comprehension Question: Are your classmates interrupting because they think your ideas are bad?

Scenario: You are sitting in your History class and space out for a minute. Your teacher calls on you to answer a question, and you didn't hear it. You ask her to repeat her question and know that she will forgive you for being distracted.
Comprehension Question: Will your teacher forgive you for being distracted?

Scenario: You and your friend are competing for a summer internship. The day of decisions arrives, and you feel a jolt of envy when you see your friend post that they got the internship. The envy curdles to despair in your stomach, until you remind yourself that one opportunity doesn't define your path, and you start to feel hopeful.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel hopeful about your future opportunities?

Scenario: While working in a group on a project, you share your ideas with your group. The other members of the group don't respond to you. You realize they were thinking about the project and didn't notice you.
Comprehension Question: Did your group ignore you on purpose?

Scenario: The science fair is next week, and you've been working hard on your project. You overheard your classmates joking that only "nerds" participate. You think about the fun you've had preparing your project and feel satisfied.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel satisfied with your science fair project?

Scenario: It's your turn to give a presentation in your language class. You stand at the front of the room and feel every pair of eyes on you. Sweat begins to trickle down your spine. You start to think everyone is judging your voice and words. You remind yourself that most people are too focused on themselves to notice small mistakes, and you feel your shoulders loosen.
Comprehension Question: Are you able to complete the presentation?

Scenario: It's the first day of school, and you have a new locker assignment. Your locker won't open, and you are getting really frustrated, until another student you know walks over and says that you have the wrong locker. You feel embarrassed, but the other student probably won't even remember.
Comprehension Question: Will the other student likely remember your locker mix-up?

Scenario: During group work, everyone seems to speak over you. You feel frustrated, thinking your ideas are not valued. Then you remind yourself that people sometimes dominate conversations unintentionally, so you start to feel patient.
Comprehension Question: Are you able to forgive your group?

Scenario: Your teacher is handing back grades for a quiz you studied really hard for. As your teacher hands back your paper, you make out the shape of a red C minus written on top, and your stomach sinks. You remind yourself that doing poorly on one quiz is an inaccurate reflection of your ability.
Comprehension Question: Does the C minus accurately reflect your overall ability?

Scenario: Your teacher asks you to collect your homework at the beginning of class. Your homework isn't in your bag, where you put it last night. Your homework must be lost. You take a deep breath and decide to tell your teacher your homework is missing. You will be fine.
Comprehension Question: Your teacher probably thinks you are...

Scenario: Your neighbors were really loud last night, so you couldn't sleep. You have a huge test this morning in your least favorite class. As you board the bus, you decide that there's no changing the past, and even though the situation isn't ideal, all you can do is your best.
Comprehension Question: Sleeping poorly before a test will probably cause you to...

Scenario: You're sitting in a class that has always been your favorite, listening to the teacher speak. You suddenly realize you don't enjoy the subject like you used to, and worry you are losing your passion. You remind yourself that motivation fluctuates.
Comprehension Question: Regaining passion for a subject is....

Scenario: You take an SAT practice test and bomb the math section. You worry you'll never get into college and feel panic tighten your throat. You remind yourself that math skills are a flexible trait.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe your math skills are fixed and unchangeable?

Scenario: You studied hard for an important test. You see that you got a lower score than you expected. You think about whether you will be able to pull your grade up with the next test, and realize this was the last test. Right now, you aren't happy, but you think about your overall course grade. You realize that you will pass.
Comprehension Question: Will you pass the course?

Scenario: You stare at a college poster in the hallway and feel your chest tighten. Your grades weren't very good in your first year of high school. When you think about applying to college, you feel good about how you've performed in school since then.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel good about how you've performed since your first year?

Scenario: You miss a few days of school due to an illness. When you come back to your first period and see the pile of makeup work waiting for you, you start to despair, thinking you'll never catch up. You remind yourself that doing one thing at a time still counts as progress, and you'll eventually be done.
Comprehension Question: Will you eventually finish your makeup work?

Scenario: You just turned in an important paper. As you're checking your submission, you notice you made an embarrassing typo in the first sentence. You recognize that this was an honest mistake and feel optimistic that your teacher will understand.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your teacher will understand the typo?

Scenario: You have a test in your history class today. You've been studying hard for it because it counts for a big chunk of your final grade. When the teacher places the test on your desk, and you look at the first question, you feel prepared.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel prepared for the history test?

Scenario: You have a lot of work to do for your history class. One of your homework assignments is to do research about a historical figure and make a well-prepared, lengthy presentation to your classmates. As you imagine yourself giving your presentation, you feel anticipation.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel anticipation about giving your presentation?

Scenario: You have a lot of homework due tomorrow. You've been procrastinating getting it done because it is going to be hard. When you think about doing your homework when you get home from school, you feel able to complete it on time.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel able to finish your homework on time?

Scenario: You get your math test back and see a low score. Your chest tightens as you think, "I'm just bad at this." You remind yourself that one test doesn't define your ability to improve.
Comprehension Question: Does one bad test define your ability to improve?

Scenario: You get an email from your school saying that new grades have been posted. You open the grade portal and see your average drop, your heart sinking a little. For a second, it feels like you’ve completely blown it. Then you remind yourself it’s just one grade, not the whole story, and you feel calmer.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel calmer after reminding yourself it's just one grade?

Scenario: You are taking a major midterm exam in one of your classes. You come across a question you're sure you've studied, but your mind is utterly blank as you try desperately to come up with the answer. After a few minutes, you decide to come back to the question later, and calmly turn to the next page.
Comprehension Question: Do you calmly move on to the next question?

Scenario: You are sitting in math class, when you suddenly realize you forgot to complete an assignment due today.  Your stomach plummets, and you imagine your grade dropping beyond repair. You take a deep breath and remind yourself that one homework assignment won't determine your grade.
Comprehension Question: Will one missed assignment ruin your entire grade?

Scenario: You are doing a complicated reading for your History class, and you have to read a chapter twice to understand what's going on. You worry that you just aren't smart enough to be in the class. You take a break from the chapter and remind yourself that confusion means you are still learning the subject.
Comprehension Question: Do you think struggling with the reading means you're not smart enough?

Scenario: Today, you will receive an important email. It will tell you whether you got accepted to or rejected from the college you really want to go to. As you think about waiting for the email, you feel excited.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel excited while waiting for the college email?

Scenario: The day before a group project is due, you notice your team misunderstood part of the project. You stay up way too late fixing the error, rereading it on your phone and still spotting tiny mistakes. You want to cry with frustration, feeling like you’ll never get it right. Eventually, you put your phone away, reminding yourself that your effort matters as much as your grade.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe your effort matters as much as your grade?

Scenario: Sitting at home, you open a blank document for a big project. You think about the upcoming due date and feel nauseous, convinced you’ll never finish in time. When you think about starting the essay, you feel prepared.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel prepared to start the essay?

Scenario: It's the night before a big exam, and no matter how hard you try, you can't seem to focus. You start to panic, wondering if you've lost your motivation forever. You remind yourself that energy comes and goes, and you probably just need to sleep.
Comprehension Question: Do you think you've lost your motivation forever?

Scenario: It's late in the evening the night before a big essay is due. Your eyes ache from staring at your computer screen, but your essay still feels far from complete. You begin to feel that nothing you do is good enough. After a few more minutes, you shut the computer, reminding yourself that sometimes trying is enough.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe that trying is enough?

Scenario: It's a warm day in spring, a few weeks before your final exam in a class. Lulled by the warmth, you zone out and realize you missed the teacher’s explanation of an important concept. For a moment, you panic, thinking you'll never catch up. When you think about going home to study the concept after school, you feel capable.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel capable of catching up on the concept you missed?

Scenario: During class, your teacher gives a presentation about how to best prepare for college applications. You listen to her recommendations and find yourself feeling nauseous, comparing your relative lack of progress to the teacher's examples. You remind yourself that not all paths to college look the same, and it's okay to not relate.
Comprehension Question: Do you think every path to college has to look the same?

Scenario: During a big test, you sit in class with your mind racing while you hear the scratch of your classmates' pencils around you. You worry you're just not smart enough and feel a heavy drop in your chest as your mind stalls. You remind yourself that everyone grasps things at different rates, and effort matters more in the long term.
Comprehension Question: Are you proud of your effort?

Scenario: As you're finishing your homework at midnight, you realize you still have a couple of math problems left. You plan to wake up a little early to finish them. While you're setting your alarm and thinking about your plan, you feel ready to wake up on time.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel ready to wake up early to finish your homework?

Scenario: You are taking the first online test in your world history class. In the middle of the test, your internet cuts out. You think about losing time on the test and feel confident in your ability to complete the test on time.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel confident you can finish the test despite the internet outage?

Scenario: You stay up late finishing an essay and still don't feel it’s perfect. Your thoughts start to spiral, asking if anything you do is ever good enough. You think this one essy is unlikley to determine your future achivement.
Comprehension Question: Will this one essay determine your future success?

Scenario: Today your top college is emailing you about whether or not you were accepted. You have a few hours to wait until you'll get the email. When you think about waiting that long, you feel excited.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel excited while waiting for the college decision?

Scenario: You are taking a test in your environmental science class. You only have ten minutes left and still have three long problems to finish. As you think about your ability to complete the test, you start to feel focused.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel focused despite the time pressure?

Scenario: During a Zoom class, you're placed into breakout rooms. When you start the discussion, your camera is on, but everyone else leaves their cameras off and their mics muted. You wonder if others will think you are motivated.
Comprehension Question: Do you leave your camera on?

Scenario: You hear your friends bragging about their dream colleges. You worry your choices seem “less impressive” and feel your stomach sink. You think your friends probably support your choice of colleges.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your friends support your college choices?

Scenario: You have been anxious about an upcoming test for class. On the day of the test, you notice that your stomach is aching. You think that the stomach ache must be from anticipation.
Comprehension Question: Do you think your stomachache is from anticipation?

Scenario: You got caught breaking a rule at school. You didn't mean to, and know that the principal will need to call your parent. You walk into their office, knowing that no matter what happens, your parents will forgive you.
Comprehension Question: Do you believe your parents will forgive you?

Scenario: Your teacher catches you texting during class and takes your phone away. When class ends, your teacher gives your phone back and reminds you not have it out during class. You think your teacher is being nice.
Comprehension Question: Was your teacher being nice?

Scenario: You hear a rumor about a dangerous incident nearby the school, and your pulse jumps. Your fingers itch to look up information on your phone. You remember the importance of waiting for facts from a trusted source, and you feel calmer.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling calmer after deciding to wait for facts from a trusted source?

Scenario: A classmate claims AI will make most jobs disappear, and your stomach dips. You imagine having fewer options than you hoped for. You remember that new skills can be learned over time, and you feel grounded.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling grounded after reminding yourself new skills can be learned?

Scenario: You're staring at a blank résumé template for a school program. You can't think of anything impressive to add, and you assume it will look boring compared to everyone else’s. You pause and remember people often forget how ordinary their early résumés are.
Comprehension Question: Is your résumé uniquely worse than everyone else's?

Scenario: You attend a presentation at school about climate change. As you sit in the dark auditorium, you feel a wave of helplessness wash over you, thinking that nothing you do will matter compared to global problems. You remind yourself that you can only control your own actions, and you feel yourself become calmer.
Comprehension Question: Do you feel calmer after focusing on what you can control?

Scenario: You and your friends are starting to talk about what you want to study in college. As you talk, you worry certain fields will be useless in a climate-shifting world. You remind yourself that careers adjust with changing conditions, and you feel exctied to pursue your interests.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling excited to pursue your interests despite a changing world?

Scenario: You're called to the stage to receive an award at your school's award ceremony. You stumble as you get up from your chair to go to the stage. When you think about everyone seeing you stumble, you feel like laughing.
Comprehension Question: Was the moment funny?

Scenario: You don't have internet access at home. You found out that you're required to do a big research project online by next week. As you wonder how you'll be able to complete the assignment, you feel comfortable in your ability to figure it out.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling comfortable in your ability to figure out the project?

Scenario: A heated debate breaks out in class about global politics. You imagine arguments only getting worse. The tension leaves you feeling energized to learn.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling energized to learn from the debate?

Scenario: You are giving a presentation to your class about your research project. You feel that your hands are shaking a little. Wondering if it is obvious, you look around and see that a few classmates have noticed. You realize that your classmates are interested in your presentation.
Comprehension Question: Are your classmates interested in your presentation?

Scenario: You have a huge assignment due tomorrow and a 2-hour practice with your team tonight. You think about skipping practice because you feel overwhelmed, but the thought triggers a wave of guilt. Your coach will probably be understanding if you miss practice to finish your work.
Comprehension Question: Will your coach probably be understanding if you miss practice?

Scenario: When a policy debate comes up online, you feel anxious that leaders won’t act fast enough. You picture being left behind by decisions out of your control. You think about the advocacy actions under your control, and you feel empowered to act.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling empowered to take action?

Scenario: During class, the topic of future job skills comes up unexpectedly. You wonder whether what you’re learning now will actually matter later. You remind yourself learning continues after school is over.
Comprehension Question: Does learning stop once school ends?

Scenario: During a school presentation about climate change, the room feels unusually quiet. You start thinking nothing you do could ever matter enough. You remind yourself that local efforts don’t work alone, and you feel energized to participate.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling energized to participate in local efforts?

Scenario: During a discussion about climate activism in class, several students speak confidently. You hesitate, worrying your ideas aren’t informed enough. You think about the strength of your beliefs and values, and you feel energized to join the conversation.
Comprehension Question: Are you feeling energized to join the conversation?
